fields.sample_size: one peri-urban settlement (Bellavista, Trujillo; about 14,000 inhabitants): census Dec 2003-Jan 2004, interviews and observations 2005, surveys Sep 2005 and Sep-Oct 2007; a second survey from Nuevo Jerusalen (2007) cited for comparison; survey size not stated
fields.effect_estimate: SEDALIB (the water enterprise) rations supply to three times a week for two hours; 46% of treated water is lost in distribution; stored water averages about 45 litres per person per day (estimate), and only 17% of Bellavista households can reach optimal access. Water from the network costs US$0.33/m3, while retail water from intermediaries costs five to eight times more, and the poorest buying from tricycle vendors pay up to 16.6 times more. Rationing is justified by the enterprise as avoiding excessive consumption; 70% of dwellings have connections but no regular supply. Descriptive; no effect estimate.
fields.effect_measure: descriptive comparison of prices and coverage (no regression)
fields.section: Full text: Introduction; Bellavista: people and water; Water and health; Conclusion; Notes 3-9 (sources)
fields.exact_location: Bellavista: people and water; Water and health

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a short case study of Bellavista, Trujillo reports rationed supply (three days a week, two hours), 46% distribution loss, only 17% of households with optimal access, and retail water at five to 16.6 times the network price; descriptive, read in full text 2026-10-04.

notes: Supplies the numeric findings (46% loss, 17%, price multiples) that the first extraction left blank; the empirical base is thin (short Local/Global Encounters piece).
